rules.rule: Use fresh agents with one bounded task each. Resume an existing agent only to rescue its own uncommitted work or for a short follow-up on the same task; never resume long-context agents for new work.
At most 5 builders plus 1 validator plus 1 steward run at a time, sized to the two build slots (C: lanes, D: rounds and canaries).
Agents report only when finished or blocked. Builds and test runs wait in the background; no interim hand-backs while waiting.

Builders follow the brief's 'Build strategy (Operator 2026-10-20)': C: SSD slot for lanes; one bundled lock hold per push (tools/lane-check.sh); whole test suites of every changed crate before READY (rule 4a); fix all visible failures then one re-run; re-run after a rebase whenever it touched the lane's crates or their dependencies.
Commit locally after every slice; push after each green bundled run. Uncommitted work at the end of an agent's turn is a defect.

Scoped rounds: the round's unit selection is the crates changed since the last finalized round plus their reverse-dependency closure (computed by the steward's selection helper from the candidate diff). Crates outside the selection keep their last PASS proof under CX-VAL-002 (the reused verdict names both commits). CX-VAL-009 re-opens are unchanged; every re-opened lane's crate is inside the selection by construction. A full-workspace union runs every third round and whenever the toolchain, Cargo.lock dependency set or round entry script changes. Codex basis: CX-VAL-011 (added 2026-10-20 with Operator approval); Studio opts in through this record.

Freeze a round when 8 or more lanes are READY or 8 hours have passed since the last freeze, whichever comes first. One fresh validator per round; it finalizes the round in the same session and never leaves a completed union unfinalized.

One batched steward sync per round, just before the freeze: builders push and file dep-requests; the steward syncs all new crates, edges and round features at once, then runs the canary on that tip. No per-push syncs unless a builder is blocked on the probe.
C: SSD lane targets stay within the Operator's 150 GB grant (140 GiB guard). Eviction of idle lane targets requires Operator approval (pending 2026-10-20).

Write governance text (ledger ops, START_LOG lines, messages) with file tools, never inlined in shell commands, so command-text hooks do not match words inside notes. Gated commands start with a leading `cd` into the Studio governance folder or a lane worktree, never the kernel root (the root pointer belongs to WP-KERNEL-012). Never reshape a command to get past a hook.
Gameplan use for Studio: pending Operator decision of 2026-10-20 (Operator suggested stopping it). Until decided, the existing hook stays in force and is not bypassed.
HANDOFF.md is refreshed at the end of every round and before any expected pause (usage limit, end of day), with current heads, running agents, READY backlog and Operator items.
